Everything in #229 that does not need a human, made into one recipe. #229 was originally written as a fifteen-item human checklist; six of those items genuinely need a human, and the rest were mislabelled. This is the rest.

Principle: spend tokens once to produce software that consumes none (#195, seed idea 3). Setup performed by an agent reading a checklist is setup that will be done differently next time.

## `just prereqs check`

Reports what is missing, one line per item, and exits non-zero if anything blocking is absent. Verified missing on this box today: `gitleaks`, the `codex` CLI, `~/.arma-cti/credentials.env`, any z.ai credential. Named refusals, never a silent pass — a check that could not run is not a check that passed (the #41 shape).

## `just prereqs credentials`

Creates `~/.arma-cti/credentials.env` at mode 0600, outside every worktree, and writes the key the human pastes. Never echoes it, never puts it on a command line, never writes it anywhere else. Idempotent, and refuses rather than overwriting an existing key without an explicit flag.

## `just prereqs sudo-script`

**Generates** a root script and prints the path; does not run it. One reviewable file covering all three root actions:

1. the `traces` pipeline and the filtered `group_by` export in `/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml` (root-owned, 644)
2. `systemctl restart otelcol-contrib`
3. the durable export directory, writable by the collector's user `otelcol-contrib` and readable by `andre`

It must be legible to someone deciding whether to run it as root. Generated to be read, not trusted. This should be the only sudo in the initiative.

## `just prereqs statusline`

Chains a quota-tap script ahead of the existing status line in `~/.claude/settings.json` (user-owned, 600 — no root needed) and passes its output through unchanged. Currently the caveman plugin's script sits there; replacing rather than chaining it would silently remove the human's status line.

The governance weakness stands and should be stated in the recipe's own output: this file is outside the repository, so nothing here can enforce or test that it stays wired. If the tap disappears, the breaker degrades to reacting to 429s.

## `just prereqs tools`

Installs `gitleaks` as a user-local binary — no sudo. Later, the `codex` CLI, and `.codex/config.toml` written to disable the off-box metrics exporter **before first use**, since Codex's `metrics_exporter` defaults to `Statsig` → `https://ab.chatgpt.com/otlp/v1/metrics`. Doing that after first use means telemetry has already left the box.

## `just prereqs plan-tier`

Attempts to read the z.ai plan tier from the platform once a key exists, and falls back to asking. #226's quota estimator needs the 5-hour and weekly caps and there is no documented machine-readable source, so this may fail — in which case it must say so plainly rather than guessing a tier.

## Also here: propose #224's bar

Compute the distribution of the gate signals from the Claude history already in the repo and **propose** a per-seat bar on #224. The human approves or moves the number; the derivation is not their work. Separate the eligible population honestly first — roughly 168 closes in 7 days are on record, but batch small-fry, docs and retro amendments are not dispatched implementation issues with a gate signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `just prereqs check` reports every item's true state, with named refusals and no silent passes
- [ ] The credentials path never exposes a key in `ps`, a log, a shell history or a committed file
- [ ] The sudo script is generated, reviewable, idempotent, and never run by an agent
- [ ] The status line is chained, not replaced; the existing output survives verbatim
- [ ] `.codex/config.toml` disables the off-box exporter, and a test asserts it
- [ ] #224 carries a proposed bar with its distribution and its population definition
- [ ] Logic in Python under pytest per ADR-0049; bash only at the seams it owns
- [ ] `just check`, `just unit` green; command table rows land with the recipe or follow through the sign-off gate

Refs #221, #229, #224, #226, #227, #195
